Subject: Spark POC: success matrix, model choices, and contingency owners

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for a productive call today. As promised, here’s a concise recap and a proposed POC plan we can iterate on. The goal is to get a 4-week trial running to validate latency, quality on your sample prompts (support and billing flows), and multilingual coverage for EN/ES/FR.

High-level proposal:
- Duration: 4 weeks (pilot env + two-week evaluation window)
- Success criteria (pass/fail checks we can automate):
  - Avg latency (95p) < 280ms for EN short utterances (<=64 tokens)
  - Intent classification accuracy >= 88% on your labeled test set
  - Response quality: human-rated NPS >= 4 on a 1-5 scale for 150 sample conversations
  - Multilingual coverage: baseline EN, acceptable degradation <=5% for ES/FR
- Model suggestion (initial): Open Llama 3 7B quantized (fp16->4-bit)
- Fallback: Mistral-Instruct 3B quantized for low-latency, lower-cost path when chipset or slot constrained
- Observability: token-level cost, per-request trace IDs, and the evaluation checklist attached

Action items (owners & timing):
1) Redwood to deliver SOW draft + evaluation checklist — owner: me (Ben) — by EOD 5/18 (attached).
2) Spark to share 200 labeled sample conversations + a prioritized prompt list — owner: Emma — by 5/20.
3) Priyom to provision dedicated trial slots and baseline infra config (autoscale policy) — owner: Priyom — by 5/22.
4) Marissa to coordinate success-rater panel and weekly readout cadence — owner: Marissa — by 5/22.

Notes on model choices and why:
- Open Llama 3 7B (quantized) provides the best tradeoff here between quality and cost for instruction-following tasks we saw in your examples.
- Mistral-Instruct 3B as fallback gives us a faster cold-start and lower memory footprint when we need to expand concurrency. We’ll do a short comparison sweep during week 0 to confirm prompts that prefer one model over another.

Risks & mitigations:
- Multilingual drop: if ES/FR drops >5% we will run lightweight fine-tune / prompt-engineering experiments and may recommend a specialized ES/FR model for those threads.
- SLA/throughput: we’ll reserve burst capacity for peak demo windows (week 3) and provide clear fallback routing rules.

Attachments: POC-SOW-draft.pdf, spark-eval-checklist.xlsx (see Drive link below).

If this looks good I’ll send a short mutual-action plan (timeline + acceptance test) and a SOW for signature.

Thanks,
